idea: A threat intelligence platform that scans the dark web for leaked corporate credentials and alerts security teams.

final_schema.proposed_solution: A threat intelligence platform monitoring dark web credential leaks.

_regression_note: The OFF_TOPIC_TERMS regression fixture (gap-closing plan Stage 6). ev-1/ev-2/ev-3 legitimately use the exact vocabulary (crypto, dark web, malware, threat intelligence) the deleted OFF_TOPIC_TERMS constant used to statically penalize -- they must rank HIGH, not be suppressed. ev-8 is genuine noise (unrelated topic entirely) and should rank low on its own lack of summary overlap, not because of any off-topic keyword filter.

evidence_items.quote: Threat intelligence firms report a sharp rise in corporate credentials leaked on dark web marketplaces this year, exposing employees to further malware campaigns.
Most large enterprise security teams already have dark web monitoring bundled into their existing SIEM and threat intelligence platforms, reducing the case for a standalone tool.
The global threat intelligence market grew an estimated 24 percent annually over the past three years, driven by rising ransomware and crypto-related fraud.
The average cost of a corporate data breach involving leaked credentials now exceeds four million dollars, according to industry incident-response data.
Three well-funded meal-kit startups targeting healthcare workers have shut down in the past two years, citing thin margins and high acquisition costs.
